title: Netflix India Hits 688 Million Views in Record-Breaking First Half of 2026
excerpt: Indian titles dominate global charts as the country rises to become Netflix's third-largest film market worldwide, behind only the US and UK.
body:
• Indian titles generated 688 million views on Netflix in January–June 2026, a record for the country
  • India is now the #1 contributor to non-English film viewing on Netflix and ranks #3 globally for overall film viewing
  • Taskaree: The Smuggler's Web became India's highest-ranked series ever on Netflix's Global Top 100 TV List
  • Made in Korea became the first South Indian film to reach #1 on Netflix's Global Non-English Films chart

Indian content on Netflix reached a new high-water mark in the first half of 2026, with titles from the country generating 688 million views between January and June, according to Netflix's latest What We Watched report released on July 17.

The data positions India as the number-one contributor to non-English film viewing on the platform and the third-largest film market globally, trailing only the United States and the United Kingdom.

A Blockbuster Slate Across Languages

Four Indian films cracked Netflix's Global Top 100 Films list during the period: Dhurandhar, Accused, Made in Korea, and Mardaani 3. Dhurandhar led the pack, amassing 37 million views to become the most-watched Indian film on Netflix during the first half of the year, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Netflix Original films showed particular strength. Five Indian originals featured in the Global Top 500 Films: Accused, Made in Korea, Kartavya, Maa Behen, and Toaster. Accused, directed by Anubhuti Kashyap and starring Konkona Sen Sharma, trended in 72 countries — the widest global reach for any Indian film on the platform.

Made in Korea, a Tamil-Korean cross-cultural drama directed by Ra. Karthik, became the first South Indian film to top Netflix's Global Non-English Films chart, reaching the Top 10 in 53 countries including markets across Latin America, South Korea, Taiwan, and South Africa.

Indian Series Travel Across Genres

Taskaree: The Smuggler's Web, headlined by Emraan Hashmi, became India's highest-ranked series on Netflix's Global Top 100 TV List and the first Indian series to claim the #1 spot on the Global Non-English TV rankings.

Five additional Indian series featured in the Global Top 500: Desi Bling, Maamla Legal Hai, India's Got Latent, Glory, and Kohrra. The reality series Desi Bling emerged as a breakout favourite, trending at #6 on the Global Non-English TV chart with 10.4 million viewing hours.

"The opportunity is clear: to take even more stories from India to audiences around the world and further strengthen India's position as one of the world's leading creative and storytelling powerhouses."

— Netflix India

The Great Indian Kapil Show continued its global run, becoming the second most-viewed Indian series on Netflix by viewing hours. Kohrra Season 2 stayed on the Global Top 10 Series list for two consecutive weeks with over 1.6 million views and 7.7 million hours watched.

What This Means for India's Creative Economy

The numbers underscore Netflix's deepening investment in India across multiple formats — feature films, premium drama, unscripted entertainment, comedy, and creator-led content. India's presence in the Global Top 10 Non-English list has become increasingly consistent, with at least one Indian title appearing in the ranking every week since 2025.

Licensed content also performed well. War drama Border 2 trended in the Top 10 Non-English Films across 16 countries with a record 11.1 million viewing hours, while Rani Mukherjee's Mardaani 3 recorded 13.7 million viewing hours.

A Growing Global Audience for Indian Stories

For the Indian diaspora, the data reflects what many have long observed: Indian storytelling is no longer a niche genre on global platforms. The breadth of content performing internationally — from Telugu action dramas to Tamil cross-cultural films to Hindi unscripted formats — suggests that overseas audiences are engaging with Indian content across languages and genres, not just marquee Bollywood releases.

What's Next

Netflix has signalled continued investment in India's content pipeline. The platform's strategy of commissioning originals across multiple Indian languages and genres appears to be paying dividends in both domestic and international viewership. With the second half of 2026 ahead, the question is whether Indian content can sustain this trajectory and push toward the billion-view mark for a full calendar year.
